en: a peep; a word of complaint

examples.ko: 선생님이 무섭게 쳐다보자 아무도 끽소리도 못 했어요.
examples.en: When the teacher gave a stern look, nobody dared to utter a peep.

examples.ko: 형 앞에서는 끽소리 못 하고 가만히 있었어요.
examples.en: In front of my older brother, I stayed quiet without daring to say a word.

examples.ko: 억울해도 끽소리 한번 못 하고 참았어요.
examples.en: Even though it was unfair, I put up with it without a single word of protest.

examples.ko: 부장님 앞에서 끽소리라도 했다가는 큰일 나요.
examples.en: If you so much as make a peep in front of the department head, you're in trouble.
No arguing, just follow me for now.

examples.ko: 그 애는 끽소리도 없이 숙제를 다 했어요.
examples.en: That kid did all the homework without a word of complaint.

explain: '끽소리도 못 하다', '끽소리 없이', '끽소리 말고'처럼 대개 부정하는 말과 함께 써요. 불평이나 반박을 조금도 못 하는 상황을 말할 때 나와요. 같은 뜻으로 '찍소리'도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 사장님이 화를 내자 직원들은 끽소리도 못 했어요.
phrases.en: When the boss got angry, the staff couldn't say a word.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무서워서나 잘못이 있어서 반박·불평을 전혀 못 하는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone cannot argue or complain at all, out of fear or because they are in the wrong.
phrases.en_equiv: not dare to say a word

explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '끽소리도 못 하다', '끽소리 없이' and '끽소리 말고'. It describes a situation where someone cannot complain or argue at all. People also say '찍소리' with the same meaning.

examples.en: The duck waddles over.
The penguins waddle along in a line.
The child toddled over to her mom.
The bicycle wobbles, so I feel uneasy.

examples.ko: 큰 가방을 메고 뒤뚱뒤뚱 계단을 올랐어요.
examples.en: I climbed the stairs unsteadily with a big bag on my back.
It's a robot that moves with a wobble like a teddy bear.

explain: '뒤뚱거리다'와 같은 느낌의 부사로, 몸이 좌우로 흔들리며 걷는 모습을 보여 줘요. 아기가 귀엽게 걷는 모습은 '아장아장'이라고도 하는데, '뒤뚱뒤뚱'은 몸이 흔들리는 것이 더 강조돼요.

phrases.en: The bike wobbles because the load is heavy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사에 '하다'를 붙여 서술어로 써요. 사람 말고 물건이 흔들릴 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 makes it a predicate. It also works for objects that wobble.

phrases.en: I'm so full that I waddle around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 무겁거나 둥글어서 흔들리며 걷는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes walking while swaying because the body is heavy or round.

phrases.en: The baby toddles along.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 작은 걸음으로 귀엽게 걷는 모습이에요. '뒤뚱뒤뚱'은 몸이 흔들리는 게 더 강조돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows a baby taking small, cute steps. 뒤뚱뒤뚱 puts more emphasis on the body swaying.

explain_en: It is the adverb with the same feel as '뒤뚱거리다' and shows a body swaying from side to side while walking. A baby's cute steps can also be '아장아장', but '뒤뚱뒤뚱' stresses the swaying body more.

examples.ko: 선생님이 설명하자 학생이 “왜 그렇게 해야 해요?”라고 반문했어요.
examples.en: When the teacher explained, the student asked back, “Why do we have to do it that way?”

examples.ko: 동생은 대답 대신 “형은 어떻게 했는데?”라고 반문하더라고요.
examples.en: Instead of answering, my younger brother fired back, “What did you do?”

examples.ko: 무례한 질문에는 침착하게 반문하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to calmly ask back when faced with a rude question.
The conversation got longer every time he questioned back.
I was startled and ended up asking back, “What did you say?”

examples.ko: 회의 중에 바로 반문하기가 어려워서 나중에 메일을 보냈어요.
examples.en: It was hard to push back right away in the meeting, so I sent an email later.

explain: '되묻다'는 잘 못 들어서 다시 묻는 경우에도 쓰지만, '반문하다'는 질문에 대답하지 않고 의문이나 반박의 뜻으로 되받아 묻는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 인용문 뒤에 '~라고 반문하다'로 써요.

phrases.example: 친구는 사과 대신 “내가 뭘 잘못했는데?”라고 오히려 반문했어요.
phrases.en: Instead of apologizing, my friend fired back, “What did I do wrong?”
phrases.nuance_ko: '오히려'를 붙이면 대답 대신 반박하듯 되받아 묻는 느낌이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 오히려 makes the sense of answering a question with a challenge clearer.

phrases.example: 그 말을 듣고 반문하고 싶었지만 참았어요.
phrases.en: I wanted to ask back when I heard that, but I held back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의문이나 반박을 되묻고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the wish to push back with a question.

phrases.en: I didn't hear well, so I asked “Pardon?”
phrases.nuance_ko: 반박이 아니라 다시 확인하려고 물을 때도 써서 '반문하다'보다 범위가 넓어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also covers asking again just to check, so it is broader than 반문하다.

explain_en: '되묻다' can also mean asking again because you did not catch something, but '반문하다' feels like answering a question with a challenging question, expressing doubt or objection. It usually follows a quote, as in '~라고 반문하다'.

examples.en: Don't just worry for nothing, take action.
I'm pointlessly going over what happened in the past.
I ended up just wasting time in vain.
I got my hopes up for no reason and ended up disappointed.

examples.ko: 부질없이 남과 비교하며 마음 상하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't hurt yourself by pointlessly comparing with others.
I just sat there sighing to no purpose.

explain: 형용사 '부질없다'의 부사형이고, 해 봐야 소용이 없다는 허무한 마음이 들어 있어요. '괜히'보다 무겁고 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: That is a pointless worry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '부질없다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective '부질없다' placed before a noun.

phrases.example: 이제 와서 후회하는 건 부질없는 짓이에요.
phrases.en: Regretting it now is a futile act.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해도 소용이 없는 행동을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for actions that are of no use.

phrases.en: It's all meaningless now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허무한 마음을 해요체로 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses a feeling of emptiness in polite speech.

explain_en: It is the adverb form of the adjective '부질없다' and carries a feeling of futility, that it won't help anyway. It is heavier than '괜히' and appears more in writing.

examples.ko: 두 후보가 토론회에서 치열한 설전을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The two candidates had a fierce war of words at the debate.

examples.ko: 가족끼리 정치 이야기를 하다가 설전이 시작됐어요.
examples.en: We were talking politics in the family and a heated argument began.
I even got into a verbal fight with my friend over something small.

examples.ko: 설전 끝에 두 사람은 결국 화해했어요.
examples.en: After the heated exchange, the two finally made up.

examples.ko: 국회에서 벌어진 설전에 많은 사람이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Many people were shocked by the verbal clash in the National Assembly.

examples.ko: 말싸움 같은 설전은 저는 별로 좋아하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't really like verbal battles like arguments.

explain: '말다툼'이 감정이 올라온 다툼이라면 '설전'은 말로 서로 주장을 주고받는 싸움이라는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '설전을 벌이다'로 쓰고 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: A war of words suddenly broke out in the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌어지다'는 일이 저절로 시작된다는 느낌이고, '벌이다'는 사람이 하는 행동에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 벌어지다 feels like it starts on its own, while 벌이다 is for what people do.
phrases.en_equiv: a war of words breaks out

phrases.example: 긴 설전 끝에 두 사람은 악수를 했어요.
phrases.en: After a long war of words, the two shook hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말싸움 뒤의 결과를 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to follow up with the outcome after a verbal fight.

phrases.en: The two traded sharp words on the broadcast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들 앞에서 말로 겨루는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when people argue with words in front of others.
phrases.en_equiv: to engage in a war of words

explain_en: '말다툼' is an emotional quarrel, while '설전' feels like a battle of words where each side argues its case. It is usually used as '설전을 벌이다' and is common in the news.

t90.ax: I don't really like verbal battles like arguments.

en: to roar; to bellow; to thunder

examples.en: The coach sharply rebuked the players for their laziness.
He sharply told the politicians to take responsibility.
The professor sternly said, 'There is a time for studying.'
At the press conference, the CEO thundered, 'Don't make excuses.'

examples.ko: 어른들이 젊은이들의 무책임한 태도를 일갈하며 나무랐어요.
examples.en: The elders sharply rebuked the young people for their irresponsible attitude.

examples.ko: 그 칼럼은 사회의 무관심을 일갈하는 글이에요.
examples.en: That column is a piece that sharply condemns society's indifference.

explain: 큰 소리로 따끔하게 꾸짖거나 핵심을 찔러 한마디 하는 것이에요. 뉴스 기사에서 '~라고 일갈했다' 꼴로 아주 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '호통치다, 한마디 하다'를 더 써요. 단순히 말하는 것이 아니라 강하고 날카롭게 말한다는 점이 중요해요.

phrases.en: He thundered, 'This is wrong.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 기사에서 누가 한 말을 인용할 때 가장 많이 나오는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form most often used in news to quote someone's sharp words.

phrases.en: Everyone went quiet at his sharp rebuke.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일갈'은 명사로도 쓰이며 강하고 따끔한 한마디를 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 일갈 also works as a noun meaning a forceful, cutting remark.

phrases.en: Father scolded the child loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '일갈하다' 대신 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 일갈하다 in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It means rebuking someone sharply, or hitting the point with one forceful remark. It appears constantly in news as '~라고 일갈했다', while in everyday conversation people say '호통치다' or '한마디 하다'. The key point is that it is not just speaking but speaking strongly and pointedly.

t90.ax: He sharply told the politicians to take responsibility.

examples.en: He cleverly hid his lie.
Ads cleverly play on people's feelings.
The culprit slyly kept avoiding the police.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 질문을 교묘히 돌려서 대답했어요.
examples.en: That person skillfully dodged the question when answering.
Some people cleverly take advantage of the rules.

examples.ko: 중요한 조건이 작은 글씨로 교묘히 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The important condition was slyly written in small print.

explain: '교묘하다'의 부사형으로, 솜씨가 좋다는 뜻도 있지만 속이거나 피하는 장면에서 꾀 있게 한다는 느낌으로 자주 어울려요. 단순히 똑똑하게 한 일에는 '영리하게', '능숙하게'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The criminal cleverly erased the traces.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교묘히'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 '교묘하게'가 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'gyomyohi'; 'gyomyohage' is heard more in speech.

phrases.en: They got around the rule by a sly method.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 잘 드러나지 않는 꾀 있는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A crafty method that isn't obvious on the surface.

phrases.en: That trick is really cunning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기본형 형용사로, 솜씨나 꾀가 놀랍다는 평가를 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The base adjective, judging skill or cunning as remarkable.

explain_en: It is the adverb form of '교묘하다'. It can mean skillfully, but it often fits scenes of deceiving or evading with a sense of cunning. For something simply done smartly, '영리하게' or '능숙하게' is more natural.

examples.ko: 한 번 이겼다고 기고만장해서 연습도 안 해요.
examples.en: He's so full of himself after one win that he doesn't even practice.
My younger sibling got cocky after being praised.
If you get too cocky, it's easy to make mistakes.
He boasted with a cocky look on his face.
The newcomer acted cocky and got scolded.
Don't get cocky just because your grades went up.

explain: 주로 '기고만장하다' 꼴로 써서, 잘나가거나 칭찬을 받고 우쭐해서 거만하게 구는 모습을 말해요. 좋은 뜻이 아니라 흉보거나 주의를 줄 때 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '우쭐하다', '으스대다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: You shouldn't get cocky just because you're a bit good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로는 이 형태로 가장 많이 쓰고, 우쭐대는 모습을 흉볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form most often used, for criticizing someone acting cocky.

phrases.en: Once he became popular, he turned arrogant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래는 아니던 사람이 점점 우쭐해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gradually becomes puffed up.

phrases.en: His cocky attitude makes his friends dislike him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주며 거만한 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe an arrogant manner.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '기고만장하다', describing someone acting arrogant and cocky after succeeding or being praised. It is negative, used for criticizing or warning, and similar words include '우쭐하다' and '으스대다'.

t90.ax: He boasted with a cocky look on his face.

en: arbitrary; dogmatic; acting on one's own judgment or beliefs

examples.ko: 팀장님이 독단적으로 일정을 바꿔서 다들 당황했어요.
examples.en: The team leader changed the schedule on his own, and everyone was flustered.

examples.ko: 독단적인 결정은 나중에 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A unilateral decision can become a problem later.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 성격이 독단적이라 의견을 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: He is so dogmatic that he hardly listens to opinions.

examples.ko: 왜 저한테 안 물어보고 독단적으로 정했어요?
examples.en: Why did you decide on your own without asking me?
His dogmatic way of talking drove his friends away.

examples.ko: 혼자 독단적으로 움직이지 말고 먼저 의논해요.
examples.en: Don't act on your own; discuss it first.

explain: 다른 사람과 의논하지 않고 혼자 판단해서 정하는 모습을 비판할 때 써요. 실제로는 '독단적인', '독단적으로', '독단적이다' 형태로 많이 말해요. 반대되는 분위기는 '민주적'이에요.

phrases.en: Don't act on your own like that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀의 의견을 묻지 않고 움직이는 행동을 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn against acting without asking the team.

phrases.en: It's hard to work with an arbitrary person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의논하지 않는 성격을 가진 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who doesn't consult others.

phrases.en: Our team leader is a bit high-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 쓰며 사람의 태도를 비판하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a predicate to criticize someone's attitude.

explain_en: It criticizes someone for deciding alone without consulting others. In practice it mostly appears as '독단적인', '독단적으로' or '독단적이다'. The opposite feel is '민주적' (democratic).

en: to be arrogant; to be haughty

examples.en: After he succeeded, he became arrogant.
An arrogant attitude drives people away.

examples.ko: 그는 말투가 너무 오만해서 친구가 없어요.
examples.en: His way of talking is so arrogant that he has no friends.
A player who stays humble even after winning is cool.
I do not want to look arrogant.
When you are arrogant, it is hard to admit mistakes.

explain: '오만하다'는 자기가 남보다 위에 있다고 생각하고 낮추어 보는 태도를 말해요. '거만하다', '건방지다'와 비슷한 말이에요. 말할 때는 '건방지다'를 더 쓰고, 오만하다는 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요. 반대로 스스로를 낮추면 '겸손하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: That person seems a bit arrogant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 느끼는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the impression someone gives from the outside.

phrases.en: You shouldn't speak arrogantly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 행동 방식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게, it describes the manner of doing something.

phrases.en: His arrogance made his friends leave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격이나 태도를 이름처럼 말하는 명사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form, naming the trait or attitude.

explain_en: 오만하다 is an attitude of thinking you are above others and looking down on them. It is close to 거만하다 and 건방지다. In speech people say 건방지다 more, while 오만하다 appears often in writing and news. The opposite, lowering yourself, is 겸손하다.

examples.ko: 허울 좋은 약속만 하고 지키지는 않았어요.
examples.en: He made fine-sounding promises but never kept them.

examples.ko: 그건 평화라는 허울 아래 이루어진 일이에요.
examples.en: That was done under the guise of peace.

examples.ko: 허울뿐인 사과는 아무 도움이 안 돼요.
examples.en: An apology that is only for show does not help at all.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 복지라는 허울을 쓰고 일을 시켜요.
examples.en: That company makes people work under the cover of 'welfare'.
The outward show may look plausible, but the inside is empty.
Do not be fooled by appearances; look at the substance.

explain: 겉만 번듯하고 속은 비어 있을 때 쓰는 나쁜 뜻의 말이에요. '허울 좋은 ~', '허울뿐이다', '~라는 허울 아래'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '겉치레'가 있어요.

phrases.en: That promise was only for show.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모양만 있고 속은 비었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something has only an outer shell with nothing inside.
phrases.en_equiv: to be nothing but a facade

phrases.example: 그는 마침내 착한 사람이라는 허울을 벗었어요.
phrases.en: He finally dropped the facade of being a nice person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거짓된 겉모습이 드러나거나 없어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a false outer image is exposed or dropped.

phrases.en: It's all show on the outside with nothing in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허울'과 비슷한 말이고, 겉만 꾸미는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that refers to decorating only the surface.

explain_en: It has a negative tone for something that looks nice outside but is hollow inside. It is used in forms like '허울 좋은 ~', '허울뿐이다' and '~라는 허울 아래'. A similar word is '겉치레'.

t90.ax: That was done under the guise of peace.

examples.en: That couple finally decided to split up.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 갈라선 이유는 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows why the two of them split up.

examples.ko: 그날 회의에서 나온 한마디 때문에 두 사람이 갈라서게 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of one remark at that day's meeting, the two ended up parting ways.
It wasn't easy to bring up the idea of splitting up.

examples.ko: 사람들이 길 양쪽으로 갈라서서 선수들을 맞이했어요.
examples.en: People stood divided on both sides of the road to welcome the athletes.

examples.ko: 오래 사귄 커플이 갈라섰다는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There's a rumor that the couple who dated for a long time have split up.

explain: '헤어지다'는 연인이나 친구에게 두루 쓰지만, '갈라서다'는 부부나 동업자처럼 오래 함께한 관계를 끊을 때 자주 써요. 길 양쪽으로 나뉘어 서는 뜻도 있어요.

phrases.example: 성격이 너무 달라서 결국 갈라서게 됐어요.
phrases.en: Their personalities were so different that they ended up splitting up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 정했다기보다 상황 때문에 관계를 끊게 되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a relationship ends because of circumstances rather than a simple decision.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 갈라선 뒤에도 가끔 연락해요.
phrases.en: Even after splitting up, the two of them still keep in touch sometimes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갈라서다'에 '-ㄴ 뒤'를 붙여 헤어진 이후의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach '-ㄴ 뒤' to talk about what happens after the split.

phrases.en: The couple argued for a long time and eventually got divorced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법적으로 부부 관계를 끝낸다는 뜻이 분명해서 '갈라서다'보다 직접적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It clearly means a legal end to a marriage, so it is more direct than 갈라서다.

explain_en: '헤어지다' is used broadly for lovers and friends, but '갈라서다' is often used when a long-standing relationship such as a marriage or partnership ends. It can also mean standing divided on either side, for example along a road.

examples.en: Don't bring it up after everything is already over.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 이제 알았냐고 친구가 뒷북친다며 놀렸어요.
examples.en: My friend teased me for being late, saying I just found out that news now.

examples.ko: 사고가 난 뒤에야 점검하는 건 뒷북치는 일이에요.
examples.en: Checking things only after an accident is acting too late.

examples.ko: 어제 나온 뉴스를 오늘 말하다니 완전 뒷북쳤네요.
examples.en: Talking about yesterday's news today, you're really behind the times.
It's pointless to make a fuss about it now.

examples.ko: 뒷북칠 생각은 없지만 한마디 해도 될까요?
examples.en: I don't mean to speak up too late, but may I say something?

explain: 일이 다 끝난 뒤에야 나서거나 뒤늦게 반응하는 사람에게 쓰는 말이에요. '뒷북을 치다'로도 쓰고, 조금 놀리거나 비판하는 말투예요. 자기 자신에게 '뒷북이지만'이라고 먼저 말하며 조심스럽게 의견을 낼 때도 있어요.

phrases.example: 회의가 끝난 뒤에 뒷북을 치면 소용없어요.
phrases.en: It's no use jumping in after the meeting is over.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒷북치다'를 띄어 쓴 형태로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form of 뒷북치다, with the same meaning.

phrases.en: It's late, but happy birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늦은 인사나 의견을 조심스럽게 시작할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way to politely begin a late greeting or opinion.

phrases.example: 뒷북치는 사람은 늘 일이 끝난 뒤에 나타나요.
phrases.en: A person who's always late to react shows up after everything is done.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늦게 나서는 사람을 조금 놀리듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tease someone who is always late to react.

explain_en: It describes someone who reacts or steps in only after everything is over. It can also be said as '뒷북을 치다', and carries a teasing or critical tone. People also say '뒷북이지만' about themselves to introduce an opinion politely.

examples.en: Please don't insult the teacher with such words.
He was accused of desecrating the flag.

examples.ko: 죽은 사람을 모독하는 글은 올리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not post writing that defiles the dead.

examples.ko: 그 작품은 종교를 모독한다는 이유로 금지됐어요.
examples.en: That work was banned on the grounds that it insults religion.
They are disrespecting our tradition.
Nobody has the right to insult him.

explain: 사람의 명예나 믿음, 소중한 가치를 깎아내릴 때 써요. '모욕하다'보다 훨씬 무겁고 심각한 말이에요. 목적어로 선생님, 종교, 국기, 죽은 사람처럼 존중받아야 하는 대상이 많이 와요.

phrases.en: Don't say things that insult religion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~는' 꼴로 뒤의 말을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '~는' form describes the noun that follows.

phrases.en: He felt he had been insulted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모독을 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who is insulted.

phrases.en: That article insulted the dead person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 일어난 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, for something that already happened.

explain_en: Use it for tearing down someone's honor, faith, or cherished values. It is much heavier and more serious than '모욕하다'. Its objects are often things that should be respected, such as a teacher, a religion, a flag, or the dead.

t90.ax: Nobody has the right to insult him.
